chunks: The two of them were saying:
Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, delegated to His Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) the affair of His creation, so that He may observe how their obedience would be.
Then he recited this verse: “Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you from, refrain.”
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hajjal, from Tha‘labah ibn Maymun, from Zurarah — similarly to it.

key_terms.أَمْرَ خَلْقِهِ: the affair of His creation, referring to the management or authority over people’s religious matters
key_terms.الرَّسُولُ: the Messenger whose commands are to be followed
key_terms.طَاعَتُهُمْ: their obedience to Allah through obedience to the Prophet
key_terms.فَانْتَهُوا: refrain, meaning desist from what he prohibits
key_terms.فَخُذُوهُ: take it, meaning accept and adhere to what he brings
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: similar to it, indicating a parallel transmission
key_terms.نَبِيِّهِ: His Prophet, meaning the Messenger appointed by Allah

ai.seo_question: How does Qur’an 59:7 show the authority of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله over the believers?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, entrusted His Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) with authority over the affairs of His creation as a test of their obedience. It supports this meaning by citing the Qur’anic command to accept what the Messenger gives and refrain from what he forbids, highlighting the binding authority of the Prophet’s command.
